newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs and pork bellies close higher.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs and pork bellies close higher.

text.p: CME lean hog and pork belly futures closed higher largely on end-of-the-week shortcovering, traders said.
"This was just a recovery rally," said one hog trader.
He and other traders noted hog futures have trended lower for many weeks and this week the lead contract dropped under 80 cents per lb for the first time since mid-April.

Traders said the market was due for an upward bounce after the long downtrend. Even when fund selling was pressuring futures early, traders pointed out there was steady scale-down commerical buying underway.
Also, since May 9, June hogs went from a close of 85.00 cents per lb to Friday morning's low of 79.375. July hogs went from 86.125 on May 9 to Friday's low of 79.70.
Cash hogs were called steady Monday with some traders relaying talk there may be fewer market-ready hogs available next week.

Pork belly futures climbed higher largely on shortcovering amid light volume. Some traders said recent news that some meat packers will reduce hog slaughter next week indicates that cash belly prices may soon firm up.
Several analysts said this week's drop in cash belly prices has increased demand by bacon processors.
In its midday carlot report, USDA quoted fresh pork bellies steady to $3.00 per cwt lower, with 12- to 14-lb portions at $83.00 per cwt.
Hogs closed up 0.050 to 1.100 cents with June up 0.050 at 80.100 cents and July up 0.325 at 80.650. Pork bellies closed up 0.275 to 1.350 cents with July up 0.275 at 86.375.
